children: shares edged higher in premarket trading Tuesday after Starship reached orbit for the first time, but investors are getting conflicting signals about what comes next for the stock.

SPCX rose about 1% before the open after Monday's Flight 14 successfully reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The mission marked a major step toward larger Starlink launches and future NASA missions, even though an engine issue forced SpaceX to shorten the flight.
Wall Street remains bullish on the longer-term opportunity.

SpaceX carries a Moderate Buy consensus based on 27 Buy ratings, five Holds and two Sells. The average analyst price target of $233.10 implies roughly 60% upside from Tuesday's cited share price of $145.47.

Bank of America analyst Ronald Epstein reiterated a Buy rating and $235 price target following the launch. He argued that Flight 14 demonstrated Starship's ability to reach orbit and deploy operational payloads.
TD Cowen also initiated coverage of SpaceX with a Buy rating and $200 price target, citing what analyst John Blackledge called a Mammoth AI & Space Opportunity.
Blackledge expects terrestrial AI compute leasing to become SpaceX's largest revenue stream as soon as the first quarter of 2027.
The near-term technical setup looks far less encouraging.
SPCX carries an overall Sell signal on the one-day timeframe, while its moving-average indicators point to a Strong Sell.
Shares were trading below the 20-day exponential moving average of $147.42, although slightly above the 50-day EMA of $145.27. The 14-day relative strength index of 48.93 remains neutral.
That creates a clear split for investors.
Technical indicators suggest momentum remains fragile, while Wall Street analysts are focused on the longer-term economics of Starship, Starlink and SpaceX's expanding AI business.

The next test is whether Flight 14's operational progress can translate into faster satellite deployment, greater launch capacity and enough revenue growth to justify Wall Street's bullish price targets.

title: SpaceX Just Sent a Strong Signal to Stock Investors
